method: Name ranking from complete parse-only census; selected full name families inspected to expose contracts missed by body thresholds. Counts are literal clauses, not expanded default arities.

reviewed_families.name: parse_time
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name in frozen census read, including heads and fallback clauses.
reviewed_families.assessment: All six clauses in two modules read. ModelAvailability accepts DateTime, ISO strings and integer Unix seconds; ModelDiscovery accepts ISO strings only, otherwise nil. The common ISO clause is real, but substituting full functions would change accepted inputs. Keep scalar conversion reuse separate from provider/model input normalization.

reviewed_families.name: parse_datetime
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name in frozen census read, including heads and fallback clauses.
reviewed_families.assessment: All eight clauses in four modules read. DecisionQuery.Cursor requires DateTime.from_iso8601 offset exactly zero and returns ok/error invalid. Comment poller returns DateTime/nil for binary input; GitHub Issues and Linear explicitly accept nil but their general clause is unguarded. Preserve cursor UTC restriction, return shapes and type guards; do not use a permissive nil-returning parser for persisted cursor validation.

reviewed_families.name: to_iso8601
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name in frozen census read, including heads and fallback clauses.
reviewed_families.assessment: All four clauses in two reset-time modules read. Both nil clauses return nil; both other clauses shift zone to Etc/UTC then render ISO. These fall below the five-line body threshold yet are true same-operation candidates. Reuse only a provider-neutral time formatting primitive if one already fits; do not unify provider reset parsing, which has distinct input policies.

reviewed_families.name: format
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name in frozen census read, including heads and fallback clauses.
reviewed_families.assessment: All twelve clauses in seven modules read. Operations include CI diagnostic prose, slot-warmth table, supervision-health delegation/formatting, CLI format-option validation, timezone-aware minute rendering and pricing boundary ISO. Sharing this name supplies no common abstraction. Preserve the existing SupervisionHealth formatter delegation rather than count it as duplicate work.

reviewed_families.name: timestamp
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name in frozen census read, including heads and fallback clauses.
reviewed_families.assessment: All 36 clauses in nineteen modules read. Family includes parsing with plain or field-tagged errors, map-field extraction plus Diagnostic, ISO serialization, string passthrough, receive/current-time fallback, no-argument clock sampling, and HEEx components with ISO/relative/timezone presentations. Do not create one timestamp function for these meanings. Matching Decision public projection ISO/nil clauses are a local codec reuse candidate; preserve DecisionHistory string passthrough, DecisionProjection narrow nil/DateTime contract, and unavailable versus utc_now fallback. UI formatting precision and timezone are surface policy.

reviewed_families.name: safe_call
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name in frozen census read, including heads and fallback clauses.
reviewed_families.assessment: All eleven definitions in eleven modules read. TUI and IssueContext collapse all failures to nil; telemetry accepts a caller fallback and catches all; Streamdeck Live/Projection catch exceptions and exits only; AddAgentSubmission preserves tagged exception/throw reasons; Presenter wraps success in ok and failures in error; ProcessReaper discards normal RPC result and returns ok even on exit; ProviderAccountGeneration catches RPC exits only. Reuse existing TUI RenderState.safe_call locally, but do not infer a universal safety helper. Preserve arity, success envelope, throws, exception detail and timeout behavior.

reviewed_families.name: normalize
reviewed_families.coverage: All 81 literal definitions/declarations named normalize read in full, including heads and fallback clauses. Additional full files read: ToolCallIdentity, JSONSafe and UnitsRow.URL; relevant Bounded URL pipeline and URI rules also inspected. This is function-family review, not full review of all transitive helpers.
reviewed_families.assessment: The name spans fingerprint canonicalization, diagnostic clipping, provider telemetry conversion, command validation, hook/webhook projections, cache inspection, JSON serialization, conversation trust filtering, opaque identifiers, pause persistence, meter schema, UI fallback and URL validation. Preserve domain contracts; spelling alone supplies no shared abstraction.
constraints: ToolCallIdentity recursively stringifies atom map keys and converts tuples to lists while retaining scalar atoms/unknown values. JSONSafe additionally handles DateTime/structs and converts non-JSON scalars. Fingerprint uses deterministic term_to_binary after normalization; replacing it with JSONSafe changes identity input semantics and requires compatibility analysis.

Decision answer/delegation/enrichment/revision/validation own different lifecycle commands, authority, optimistic version/sequence checks and record-specific errors. Share validation primitives without erasing command policy.
LiveConversation drops tool/system/untrusted-user shapes; HookEvents retains raw map with classification. Neither is a generic trusted-event sanitizer.

Provider meter normalization validates snapshot/patch/tombstone schema with account-generation metadata; headless usage dispatches through provider adapters into envelopes/coverages. Do not conflate measurement semantics.
OpaqueIdentifier validates bounded allowed characters and unchanged redaction, unlike credential trim-to-nil or diagnostic clipping.

UnitsRow.URL accepts http/https default ports, empty/no query, matches issue identity and strips fragments. BuildOrder.Bounded.github_issue_url_for uses bounded HTTPS-only nil-query/nil-fragment GitHub validation. Sharing requires an explicit URL policy decision.
Cache inspector preserves false/zero/empty-list body presence and distinguishes data_source from processing source; truthiness-based generic normalization would lose that meaning.
Invalid TicketObservation input produces an unknown observation; meter input rejects schema; webhook returns error/drop; UI emits domain fallbacks. Preserve these different failure meanings.
Webhook ModeRegistry and ModeTable share trim/lowercase repo string clauses below the body threshold; ModeTable also has a nonbinary fallback. Whole-function substitution must preserve input policy.

reviewed_families.name: atomic_write
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name read from the frozen snapshot.
reviewed_families.assessment: All six literal definitions in six modules read. Four domain wrappers already delegate to Fs.atomic_write; Fs is the shared primitive, not a sixth redundant implementation. ToolResultSpill adds random names, exclusive staging-file creation, permission/sync, destination absence and workspace containment checks with final cleanup. Replacing it directly with Fs would drop preconditions and change the return from {:ok,path} to :ok.
constraints: PackStatus creates directories and logs failures; membership FileOps rejects nonregular/symlink destinations; Checkpoint maps errors to checkpoint_write_failed; RetiredFloor is a thin option wrapper.
Fs uses a unique-integer temporary suffix and optional fsync/mode. Its generic writer is not the spill policy boundary.
Read Fs and membership FileOps fully, plus spill write/sync/destination helpers. This is no durability certification or filesystem-race test; no saving measured.

reviewed_families.name: control_api_call
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses for this exact name read from the frozen snapshot.
reviewed_families.assessment: All six definitions in six orchestrator modules read. Interrupts, PriorityControl and Slots share the same fixed5000ms wrapper; OperatorMessages and RemoteControlMode accept timeout parameters. PauseResume instead reads a configured timeout and distinguishes timeout, noproc/nodedown and other call failures.
constraints: Extracting a common transport wrapper can preserve explicit timeout and error-mapping policy. Do not replace PauseResume with the generic catch-all unavailable mapping.
The same availability precheck does not eliminate a process-exit race; existing catches are necessary.

These families overlap body-census candidates, so do not count the identical wrappers as new savings or independent duplicate opportunities. Caller-wide runtime behavior is not established by this family read.

reviewed_families.name: age_label
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal clauses for this exact name read from the frozen census/source.
reviewed_families.assessment: Read all21clauses in six modules. Inputs include seconds, milliseconds and age_ms maps; outputs vary from raw milliseconds to rounded units, mixed minute/second precision and pluralized days. Missing input returns explicit unknown strings except ProviderMetersPresenter, where it returns nil. Analytics also has a source-freshness threshold before showing elapsed time.
constraints: Do not substitute helpers by name: converting milliseconds twice or losing a missing value changes meaning.
Display precision and text are surface policy. Share unit conversion only with explicit input units and preserve unavailable versus zero.
No whole-surface rendering audit or live user-visible age assertion performed.

reviewed_families.name: freshness_label
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal clauses for this exact name read from the frozen census/source.
reviewed_families.assessment: Read all25clauses in six modules. RunSummary, CurrentRunOutcomes, UsageSummary and ProviderMeters map stale to Healthy; ConversationDrawer uses current and Stale; GitHubCache maps stale to older and stringifies other values. UsageSummary adds empty; ProviderMeters has no unavailable-specific label.
constraints: These four stale mappings corroborate only a subset of existing web-occ-09; do not create a duplicate finding or certify its complete nine-site claim.
A shared presenter policy could eliminate copy drift, but choosing a label is an explicit behavior decision. Preserve empty, partial, unavailable and unknown distinctions.
Read call sites retaining status alongside label in ProviderMeters and CurrentRunOutcomes; label collapse does not prove the underlying status atom was lost.

reviewed_families.name: count_label
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal clauses for this exact name read from the frozen census/source.
reviewed_families.assessment: Read all18clauses in six modules. Families include integer-or-dash, noun pluralization, loaded-versus-total, partial counts with plus suffix, and ticket availability/truncation/search match summaries. GitHubCache special-cases misses; DecisionLatency's pluralizer does not.
constraints: Do not replace partial count N+ or truncated at-least-N with an exact integer.
Preserve unsupported tracker separately from unavailable and search matches separately from total.
These are selected function contracts, not a claim of current malformed-input or rendering failures.

reviewed_families.name: start_link
reviewed_families.coverage: All122literal definitions read in two bounded source batches;438summed source-span lines. This is not complete module or callback review.
reviewed_families.assessment: Most definitions delegate to GenServer startup, but the family also includes Agent, Supervisor, DynamicSupervisor, Phoenix.PubSub and domain facade delegates. Repeated conventional startup syntax is not evidence that the domain processes should share an implementation or package.
constraints: Preserve registration policy: fixed module names, caller-overridable defaults, unregistered startup, derived via/slot names and facade-owned names are not interchangeable.

Some wrappers pop :name before passing init options; others pass it through. Financial caches construct map state while most owners pass opts. Do not unify by textual shape without init-contract review.

DecisionStore validates start options before launching; PubSubBoot waits for old names to release; HTTPServer installs a URL callback and can return :ignore; LiveConversation derives restart-announcement policy from the name.
Existing facade delegates already express ownership; do not count them as duplicate implementations. The two-line OTP call is often the simplest appropriate boundary.
No framework nil-name behavior, runtime startup failure, process-count saving or transitive boot correctness asserted. Exact-body overlap is non-additive.

reviewed_families.name: terminate
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal clauses read from the frozen source, including fallbacks and delegates; no transitive whole-module coverage implied.
reviewed_families.assessment: All42literal clauses in36modules read. The family includes OTP callbacks plus explicit task/LiveView lifecycle helpers. Shared callback spelling does not establish shared resource ownership or safe cleanup order.
constraints: Keep owned versus injected writer distinction in DecisionMetrics; graceful flush/checkpoint paths do not prove crash durability or execution after kill.
Orchestrator cleanup uses drain:false to avoid latching the application reaper during supervised restart; do not replace it with application shutdown semantics.
Claude telemetry explicitly unlinks/stops/monitors its listener; opencode closes the port before reaping descendants; financial cache clears pending tasks before stopping its owned supervisor.
UI cleanup includes terminal restoration, relay/voice shutdown and voice-lease release. A no-op fallback is not a missing cleanup finding without proving acquired ownership.
Function spans only: transitive helper behavior, exception safety and shutdown timeout sufficiency are not certified.

reviewed_families.name: subscribe
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal clauses read from the frozen source, including fallbacks and delegates; no transitive whole-module coverage implied.
reviewed_families.assessment: All45literal clauses in38modules read. Thin Phoenix.PubSub wrappers coexist with Exchange pattern validation, durable Executor subscription-state updates, generation-scoped provider streams, authenticated FinancialData subscriptions, explicit-pid ledger subscriptions and monitored workspace ownership waiters.
constraints: Preserve caller-self versus explicit recipient semantics. WorkflowStore's signature accepts a pid but its body subscribes the calling process; do not treat it as equivalent to UsageLedger's explicit-pid registration without caller review.
Ticket detail/history subscribe to identity and reset topics; LiveConversation canonicalizes source and subscribes with restart handling; these are richer than one topic subscribe.
Provider account/meter subscriptions resolve current generation before binding. FinancialData authorizes context and obtains subscription identity before replacement.
Some optional observability wrappers catch failures and return ok; account/financial routes return unavailable/authentication errors. A generic catch-and-ignore wrapper would change the contract.
Common one-line PubSub calls are already calls to the shared transport. Do not count wrappers as duplicated transport implementation or claim savings from deleting them.

reviewed_families.name: health
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses read from frozen census/source; supporting helper and caller graphs not fully reviewed.
reviewed_families.assessment: All44clauses in27modules read. The family spans direct GenServer/backend getters, projection field access, HTTP health probing, listener-binding coverage, snapshot availability and reason-bearing UI projections. Common spelling does not supply one health enum or result shape.
constraints: CurrentRunProjection.Value maps available/writable to healthy and stale/partial/unknown to degraded, while OutcomeSnapshot.SourceState maps partial/stale to partial and has a healthy fallback. Preserve each input domain before proposing a common mapper.

RunSummary.Status combines invalid-run, source health, freshness, weight and truncation reasons; WeightFacts applies availability before stale/race policy. These are aggregate policies rather than interchangeable scalar helpers.
ProviderMetersPresenter preserves state, failure, timestamps, failure count and age alongside labels. Do not replace that projection with a single status string.

Facade delegation already supplies reuse. DeliveryLog calls its wrapper with writable as fallback, while PackStatus catches exits as unavailable; caller/wrapper review is required before declaring either contract correct or equivalent.
Overlap with web-occ-20 is partial corroboration of vocabulary differences, not a new independent defect.

reviewed_families.name: freshness
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definition clauses read from frozen census/source; supporting helper and caller graphs not fully reviewed.
reviewed_families.assessment: All28clauses in19modules read. The family includes delegation, source maps, reconciliation metadata, scalar normalization, age thresholds, expiry deadlines and UI status/label projection.
constraints: TicketHistory and TicketActivity use age > threshold; cache entries use age >= stale/expired thresholds. Equality is observable and must not change accidentally during consolidation.
Provider meter reconciler treats no expires_at as fresh and expiry equal to now as stale; this is not equivalent to an observation timestamp being absent, which other domains represent as unknown.
Membership runtime returns reconciliation status plus last-observed/recovered/reconciled metadata and pending terminal verification, not a generic elapsed-age result.
RunSummary freshness aggregates normalized per-source states; UnitsRow preserves per-source freshness with unknown fallbacks. Shared types can document contracts without collapsing policies.
No runtime stale-data incident, input reachability proof or savings claimed from this function-family read.

reviewed_families.name: positive_integer
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal clauses/declarations read from frozen census/source, with targeted provider model-helper reads; not complete transitive modules.
reviewed_families.assessment: All33clauses in17modules read. Five simple positive-integer-or-nil families match, but others return ok/value, ok alone, field-tagged errors, diagnostics, usage prose or defaults. Provider meter input also enforces a maximum source version.
constraints: CI poller and PullRequests accept complete positive numeric strings but return different errors; GraphqlErrors uses Integer.parse and accepts remaining suffix text. Preserve that distinction unless intentionally changing parsing policy.
RemoteControl and PauseContainment accept supplied defaults; ControlLifecycle uses a fixed history-limit default; projection State reads a keyword key before validating.
A shared predicate can express integer >0, but normalization, parsing, bounds and fallback selection remain explicit caller contracts.
No caller-wide malformed-input reachability or production failure asserted. Numeric-prefix acceptance is observed source behavior, not automatically classified as a bug.

reviewed_families.name: parse
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal clauses/declarations read from frozen census/source, with targeted provider model-helper reads; not complete transitive modules.
reviewed_families.assessment: All39literal definitions/declarations in21modules read. The name spans logs, GraphQL connections, bounded markers/labels, reset-time hints, model names/lists, config, query cursors/params, dotenv, tool calls, budget holds, dates, CPU counters, tmux streaming and versions.
constraints: Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter model-list parse bodies match, but inspected model helpers retain distinct display-name, context-length and pricing conversion. Shared envelope iteration must accept an explicit provider converter rather than replace domain parsing.
Claude and Codex reset parsers differ in trimming and timezone parameters; previously reviewed shared formatter clauses do not make reset-time grammars equivalent.
Cursor decoding preserves byte bounds, base64/JSON shape and normalized identity/date errors. Tmux parse carries remainder state between chunks; neither belongs in a generic stateless parser.
Fallbacks include nil, empty list, error atom, tagged errors, diagnostic warnings and unavailable. Keep consumer expectations explicit.
Bodyless default-argument declarations are counted as literal census entries, not extra implementations. Transitive parser completeness and safety are outside this family read.

reviewed_families.name: snapshot
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: The name spans synchronous process reads, facades, pure projections, provider validation, ETS observations, file-backed reads, command decoding and operational sampling. Thin process wrappers already share GenServer; a universal snapshot helper would erase domain contracts without establishing common ownership.
constraints: Preserve process identity, per-call timeouts and failure envelopes: AttachPool uses 1000ms with an empty-shaped fallback, Slot uses 2000ms with status unavailable, while other process accessors propagate exits or return domain-specific unknown/unconfigured values.

Preserve authority epoch, generation, repository and tracker identity, provider binding and authentication scope. TicketDetail validates response identity before constructing a snapshot; Claude and Codex validate distinct provider payload contracts.

Preserve freshness, health, provenance, truncation, denominator generation and observed-at fields when decomposing projections. CurrentRunProjections already owns shared summary/outcome reads; matching facade names do not imply duplicate state stores.

ETS metrics and cache reads, multi-source BudgetMap aggregation and sequential runtime sampling do not establish a single transactional observation merely by returning one map. Package APIs must document observation consistency rather than assume it from the name.

CredentialHeadroom returns an empty map on ArgumentError; Budget returns empty-shaped admission state on command/decode failure; Quota and other sources expose explicit unknown/unavailable envelopes. These differences require consumer and policy review before classifying a defect or standardizing fallback behavior.
ProviderMeterSource uses redacted_snapshot for presentation. Preserve that disclosure boundary; raw provider-store access and externally rendered snapshots are not interchangeable.

reviewed_families.name: load
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read, plus six checkpoint/block/manifest/floor load helpers and complete JsonStore and GlobalPauseStore modules. Transitive consumers and decoders remain outside this family pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: The name covers persistent recovery, Ecto type loading, configuration/environment effects, snapshot intake, process access and UI data projection. A narrower bounded JSON artifact reader is a candidate within persistence; one generic domain loader is not supported.
constraints: UsageAggregate.Checkpoint, UsageCompaction.Block and Manifest repeat regular-file/size/symlink checks and JSON/decode pipelines. Their from_record functions and error labels remain domain-specific. Shared mechanics would accept an explicit decoder and policy, not unify record schemas.

Zero-byte regular files are missing in aggregate checkpoint, compaction block/manifest and retired floor, but ledger checkpoint and membership checkpoint pass them to JSON decoding. Preserve or explicitly migrate this difference; a universal empty-file default would change recovery behavior.

Preserve size bounds, symlink rejection, missing/corrupt distinctions and decoding errors. RetiredFloor collapses load_regular failures to invalid_retired_floor; other loaders preserve atom errors, while membership preserves decoder/read reasons. Existing JsonStore.read has neither lstat/type checks nor a byte limit and is not a drop-in equivalent.

GlobalPauseStore returns an error on unreadable/invalid persisted state, with missing state separately defaulted. CIApprovalStore, model stores and some caches choose empty fallbacks. Failure policy belongs to the owning domain; this pass does not establish downstream fail-closed behavior or classify existing differences as bugs.

Membership recovery combines checkpoint, journal, degraded marker and terminal-verification state before permitting writes; ledger recovery respects retired positions and segment/checkpoint health. Do not replace these state machines with a generic read-or-empty helper.

Keep environment loading side effects, SessionHandle backend/host/identifier validation, workflow legacy-path rejection and analytics current-versus-prior session selection separate from storage mechanics.

Pre-read lstat and later File.read are visible separate operations. This review does not prove race resistance, crash durability or measurable savings; retain these as validation obligations for any proposed shared reader.

reviewed_families.name: fetch
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: The name spans network pagination, cache-only reads, provider context, map access, local catalogs, authenticated financial data and static assets. Several provider context wrappers already delegate to one owner.
constraints: FinancialData.fetch checks access identity and source validity, and evicts stale configuration on authentication failure; its cache call carries context and identity. ControlCenterCache has a similar infinite-timeout process wrapper without that public contract. Do not substitute one wrapper based on name or message shape.

OpenIssueSnapshot uses caller max age and returns none on absence/staleness; ResourceStore uses body fetched_at rather than last processing time and returns version/source/full-body metadata; CycleFetchCache delegates to a cycle-scoped cache when present. Preserve cache population, clock and provenance semantics.

CI polling normalizes/deduplicates targets and returns an empty result before further work; comment polling additionally filters positive numbers and resolves repository/token before reducing query chunks. A common batch envelope must preserve these validation and credential boundaries.

Tickets validate configured identity and fetch relationships before constructing a snapshot. Provider-account context is reference scoped and supplies binding/authority/topic; Claude and Codex already share its implementation.

Keep result shapes distinct: complete ProviderResult with diagnostics, ticket snapshot, HTTP status errors, unsupported source, stale workflow path, miss/none and static-asset media type. This family pass does not establish transport or authorization correctness transitively.

reviewed_families.name: get
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: The name mixes map retrieval, tagged field presence, stateful process reads, generation-index reuse and validated Decision queries. Existing MapAccess delegation does not imply that every dual-key helper has equivalent semantics.
constraints: Protocol.MapAccess.get uses atom_value || string_value, so false and nil trigger fallback. DecisionAnswer, DecisionEvent, DecisionRevision, DecisionValidation and projection Value helpers use Map.get defaults, preserving a present false or nil. Consolidation must explicitly select presence or truthiness behavior.
Codex.RateLimits.get returns Map.fetch tagged results and prioritizes string-key presence before an optional atom key; it is not interchangeable with a value-or-nil accessor.
CurrentRunProjection.Value and UnitsRow.Value both support non-map fallback but use different default values (empty map versus nil). Preserve defaults and explicit third arguments.

MembershipCache reuse requires matching run and generation and a valid index shape. DecisionQuery normalizes IDs and preserves health/scope, while DecisionAPI applies encoding policy; these are domain boundaries rather than generic map reads.

Process get calls differ in failure policy: Workspace.Ownership.Store wraps exits as store_unavailable, DecisionStore propagates calls, and OpenAICompat.Session reads Agent state. No caller-visible bug or safe migration is established merely by observing these differences.

reviewed_families.name: lookup
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Lookup spans indexes, ETS, registries, processes, pricing intervals and view rows. Repeated search syntax is weaker evidence than the key, liveness, health and result contracts.
constraints: Outcome membership index distinguishes ambiguous_identity from not_current_member and includes repository scope. UnitsRow lookup compares normalized tracker identities; presenter lookups search rendered tokens. Do not replace these with an unscoped identifier search.

Sessions can be located by identifier alone or identifier plus base URL; both check process liveness. SlotRegistry validates a positive index and checks liveness. These observations do not promise the returned process remains alive after lookup.

ETS-backed readers differ in unavailable handling, TTL/identity checks and table ownership. ActiveTurns ensures its table before lookup, ReadCache delegates serving policy and catches ArgumentError as miss, and ResourceStore uses its own with_table fallback.

RetainedSnapshot gates reads on store health; provider-account registry preserves tombstones and never-observed unknown state; ProviderMeters.lookup is an existing snapshot alias. Missing, unknown and unavailable are not one generic nil result.
PriceTable lookup validates catalog version and date, chooses an exact series and pricing interval, and returns expiry. This is a domain query, not a shared key-value accessor.
Presenter row searches have similar envelopes but different row/token representations. Shared mechanics remain optional pending caller and representation review; no new defect or savings count.

reviewed_families.name: topic
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Topics include fixed channels, repository/identity-derived routes, provider generation routes and hashed conversation keys; shared string construction does not establish shared subscription scope.
constraints: Graph projection distinguishes catalog repository from selected identity; ticket detail uses cache_key(identity), ticket history uses github_key(identity), and resource events include type/owner/repository/id. Preserve the key derivation and namespace together.

LiveConversation hashes the term-encoded value and includes a version and kind; graph/detail/history routes encode terms directly. These are different representations, not evidence of an interchangeable generic identifier encoder.

Provider meter routes include provider/backend/generation; financial data routes include configuration and connection generations. Preserve invalidation and connection scope across package boundaries.

ResourceEvents returns nil on an invalid key; provider meters require a nonempty binary generation. A shared topic builder must not silently widen accepted inputs or turn invalid input into a shared channel.

Tickets, hooks, takeover alerts and Executor-command attention use different identifiers and separators; Executor-command attention includes a decision digest. Subscriber and publication matching require cross-reference review before changing any format.

reviewed_families.name: broadcast
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Many wrappers already call Phoenix.PubSub, while domain-specific choices govern payloads, routing, optional availability and failures. A common transport exists; another universal wrapper is not justified by the name alone.
constraints: OpenTicketSource broadcasts generation/status rather than the full listing; history and ad-hoc source broadcast snapshots. Preserve notification-versus-state semantics and require subscribers to re-read where the contract uses invalidation.

DebugLog uses local_broadcast on a global route and an identifier route, while most others use broadcast. LiveConversation publishes to source and optional generation-handle routes; GraphProjection distinguishes reset, generation and health and calls after_broadcast.

CacheHistory and QuotaHistory have matching catch-and-ignore wrappers around domain-specific module attributes. ResourceEvents instead routes failures to unavailable; LiveConversation asserts the first publish result. Preserve failure reporting rather than replacing all wrappers with best-effort success.

Presence checks before publishing do not guarantee the PubSub process remains available through the call. Some wrappers catch exceptions/exits and others only test Process.whereis. This family review does not classify a race as a reached production defect.

Provider-account generation iterates topic/snapshot/change triples and attaches change metadata; provider meters delegate to do_broadcast. Envelope shape and redaction require their domain owners, not just shared routing syntax.

reviewed_families.name: generation
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: The name includes owner-specific process reads, tuple/struct access, a composite source map, a namespaced planning value and random access-generation tokens. A universal counter abstraction is unsupported.
constraints: CurrentRunSummary and outcomes already delegate to CurrentRunProjections; other facades delegate to membership, provider-meter, usage aggregate or ledger owners. Shared accessor syntax is not evidence that these stores share one invalidation clock.
UnitsRow.Sources returns a map of membership/status/activity/decision/issue generations. Preserve the vector of independent sources rather than replacing it with one scalar.
FinancialDataAccess.Generation creates a 32-byte cryptographic random value encoded as URL-safe base64. It is not a numeric monotonic counter, and equality/revocation scope must remain explicit.

PlanningSource adds a nonnegative membership generation to a module-defined base and falls back to that base. LiveConversation.Source extracts the generation from a tuple also carrying identity/run/attempt/session/backend scope.
These accessor reads do not establish increment, persistence, reset or collision contracts. Review owner transitions and consumers before claiming generation unification or correctness.

reviewed_families.name: refresh
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Refresh covers asynchronous requests, synchronous process calls, pure projection aging, history merging, file/network catalog refresh, UI selection rotation and protected reads.
constraints: AdHocSource, GraphProjection and PackStatus use casts; CurrentRunProjections uses a configured call timeout and CodeOwners uses 30000ms. A cast accepting a request is not completion evidence, so common API naming must preserve receipt versus completed-result semantics.

OpenTicketSource attaches view-originated provenance to the cast. UsageRuntime checks authorized context and ready scope before fetching, otherwise demotes or reconciles without a protected read. Preserve these origin and authorization boundaries.

ProviderMeters.Reconciler refresh recomputes window/plan freshness and health from existing observations; it does not fetch a new observation. PlanningSource refresh is a no-op and TicketContextSelection rotates an open selection request. These do not share an IO refresh contract.

Ticket history merges retained and newly read entries and combines source and retained truncation. StreamdeckLogs preserves selected events and view offsets. Preserve continuity and truncation rather than replacing state wholesale.

AgentLogModal marks a disappeared running target unwritable while refreshing historical content; TrackedSet excludes deactivated rows before reset. Refresh can revoke authority, not merely update presentation.

ModelLabelRefresh uses bounded async tasks killed on timeout; ModelDiscovery records failed attempts; RepoBase emits ready/error after refresh steps. These effect and failure policies require their owning domains.

reviewed_families.name: observe
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Observe spans immutable transformations, synchronous state changes, asynchronous quota telemetry, credential reconciliation, account continuity, persistence, task dispatch and usage publication. The verb does not guarantee a read-only operation.
constraints: CurrentRunMembership carries identity, lifecycle, observation time and source through a synchronous call with a default 60000ms timeout. MembershipLifecycle converts failures into an explicit membership_observation_failed result; quota observers instead cast and tolerate exits.

Budget observe reconciles a lease using the same credential identity as admission before recording the response. CredentialHeadroom stores keyed resource windows and suppresses failures so observation cannot fail the request. Preserve identity and failure isolation separately.

Claude account observation recovers a retained binding and transitions trusted auth state; unknown auth loses continuity. ModelAvailability serializes load/merge/write by path using global.trans. Neither belongs behind a nominally read-only observer interface.

ReadyForReviewTransitions reduces and prunes observations, saves changed state and then replaces the in-memory ledger. Preserve persistence ordering and change detection; this pass does not establish crash consistency.

ProviderMeterProbe batches provider work with bounded tasks and records results; ProviderMeterRefresh avoids overlapping probes while a monitor reference exists. Keep task ownership, timeout and inflight suppression explicit.

OpenAICompat.MeterAdapter emits a patch with binding/source version and ignores ingester failure; Headless.Emitter normalizes and publishes envelopes with skip-on-error behavior. Best-effort observability is not equivalent to durable acceptance.

TurnProgress compares a witness with the previous non-nil witness and counts repeated values. DecisionMetrics.Sample advances last_observed_at via latest; neither makes a generic observation synonymous with forward progress.

reviewed_families.name: write
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations and complete Fs module read; transitive codecs, synchronization callbacks and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Write spans append logs, temporary hook configuration, recovery markers, bounded artifacts, model state, executor claims and ETS publication. Existing Fs.atomic_write supplies a narrower mechanism; domain write contracts remain distinct.
constraints: Fs.atomic_write stages a sibling file, optionally sets permissions and syncs the file descriptor, then renames and cleans up on returned failures. It does not create parents or invoke sync_filesystem; atomic replacement alone is not proof of directory-entry crash durability.

ModelAvailability and ModelDiscovery both create unique temporary JSON files and rename them. Discovery additionally calls forget_memo through tap on the rename result, including error results. A shared write path must preserve or deliberately revise that invalidation policy; neither visible wrapper cleans up rename failures.

Upgrade.State also stages and renames but explicitly removes its temporary file on returned write/rename failures. BalanceBaseline writes directly and maps exceptions/catches to error. These differences are candidates for policy review, not automatically interchangeable implementations.

Membership markers validate reason or bounded recovery record, write atomically, verify the final file and invoke a sync callback. Empty terminal-verification keys remove the marker instead. RetiredFloor includes a checksum and synchronization callback; preserve ordering and removal semantics.

Compaction block and manifest enforce size limits, call Fs with fsync and mode 0600, and map failures to domain-specific errors. Ledger checkpoint checks writable_path and encodes under limits before write_encoded. Keep codecs, bounds and error classification outside a generic byte writer.

AgentEventLog appends NDJSON then Markdown under a log lock and tolerates failures; this visible sequence is not a two-file transaction. EventPublicationLog ignores the workspace parameter, uses its publication path and returns explicit failures, preserving the separate publication-evidence boundary.

CurrentRunProjections.Checkpoint maps callback failures and skips nonbinary run IDs; SnapshotPublisher writes ETS with a monotonic version and returns success if the table is absent. Neither is a generic filesystem operation.
This pass overlaps prior atomic_write and raw persistence reviews; count no additional independent defect or LOC saving without reconciliation and caller validation.

reviewed_families.name: request
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Request includes CLI query construction, process calls, provider HTTP configuration, injected transport calls and control lifecycle transitions.
constraints: Analytics validates date range and ordering; Commands validates filter/query combinations; BuildOrders validates root; Units serializes a previously selected scope. These are domain query builders, not equivalent request transports.

ControlLifecycle validates attributes, binds request ID to intent, distinguishes duplicate same-intent requests from conflicting reuse, and supersedes pending work for the issue. Preserve idempotency and conflict semantics independently of transport completion.

TicketDetailCoordinator carries view-originated provenance. DecisionStore forwards options and an explicit timeout. A successful process call must be interpreted through its handler contract rather than assumed to mean requested external work completed.

Anthropic and OpenAI model-catalog builders require nonempty keys but use different headers; Anthropic includes its API version. OpenRouter delegates optional header construction. Keep provider authentication policy explicit.

CIReadiness pins credential identity in the request; OpenAICompat.Transport optionally acquires a backend concurrency slot and otherwise returns a result/metadata tuple. These are policy-bearing wrappers, not redundant calls.

OpenAICompat.Config uses a 300000ms receive timeout with retries disabled and returns status/body/normalized headers. Opencode.ApiClient also disables retries but classifies 2xx, HTTP errors and transport errors differently. Preserve response and retry contracts.

ElevenLabs quota maps all raised/caught request failures to probe_failed, while other injected request calls can propagate failure. Tmux mock transport sends to a process then waits for its own response timeout. None supports a universal request error envelope without caller review.

reviewed_families.name: source
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Source spans constant provider labels, validated provenance, public attribution, health/freshness envelopes, pricing URLs, fallback inputs and accounting keys.
constraints: BuildOrders source distinguishes empty/available/stale/invalid/unavailable and carries observation age, completeness and reasons. Commands explicitly has unknown freshness and no timestamp; Units derives age and truncation from its catalog. Do not invent freshness by normalizing these to one default.

DecisionApi.PublicProjection delegates sanitization and exposes only agent_id; DecisionProvenance validates an allowed source. Preserve the disclosure boundary separately from internal provenance validation.
UsageLedger.CounterPolicy returns source, source_version and counter_scope from the envelope or money record. Those fields form accounting identity, not merely a display label.

PriceTable.Validator accepts HTTPS URLs with a nonempty host; PriceTable.Data selects provider-specific source constants. This is different from enum-valued meter sources and headless adapter source accessors.

TicketHistoryNormalizer permits specific event kinds and normalizes opaque names. UnitsRow.Sources selects atom/string keys using truthiness fallback, whereas CurrentRunProjections.SourceFallback delegates to Value.get. Preserve invalid-input and false/nil behavior.
Constant accessors can remain owned by the protocol/provider that defines them. No new duplicate defect or saving is established by identical accessor bodies.

reviewed_families.name: record
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive persistence, queue and consumer contracts are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Record spans pure serialization, bounded in-memory history, synchronous store calls, asynchronous telemetry, lifecycle mutation and append persistence. Its name cannot serve as proof of durable recording.
constraints: RunTelemetry gates recording and tolerates failures; Writer.record calls enqueue_cast and returns ok, while BrokerTimeout also casts and returns ok. Preserve enqueue versus persistence distinctions and verify writer receipts before treating success as durable evidence.
Checkpoint record functions construct versioned/checksummed maps; DecisionMetrics.Log builds a map; RequestLog builds cost/identity fields. These functions do not persist those records themselves.

Deduplicating DecisionMetrics.Collector correlates attention, normalizes facts, calls Writer.persist, then updates samples and seen window. The visible call return is not matched here; review the writer contract before drawing conclusions about retry/durability behavior.

BranchRefStore and TakeoverAlert.Store use synchronous calls with different validation/timeouts. MembershipLifecycle filters for joinable tracker identity before observing. Preserve scope and failure behavior rather than routing all records through a universal fire-and-forget sink.

ProgressTracker clamps and bounds samples; StreamDiagnostics normalizes and retains a bounded tail per port; AddAgentSubmission updates an accumulated result. These are in-memory transformations with unrelated ownership.

Webhook DeliveryLog updates entries, persists a record and enforces retention; DaemonLifecycle updates a control journal but rescues exceptions. Retention and diagnostic failure policy remain domain-owned.

SaturationSentinel.record appends JSON but does not match the File.write return before returning ok. This is a static candidate for caller/failure review, not a verified production loss claim or an additional deduplicated defect.
No durable-delivery guarantee, generic recorder abstraction or measurable saving is established by this family pass. Reconcile overlap with existing telemetry/persistence findings.

reviewed_families.name: resolve
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; transitive helpers and consumers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: Resolve spans tool-call identity, closing asks/attention, configuration defaults, model selectors, path containment, process identity, port selection, retained facts and historic pricing. It does not imply a pure lookup or one common fallback policy.
constraints: Asks validates input then enters a store lock; DecisionAttention makes a synchronous resolve call; ExecutorCommandAttention reads a marker before maybe_resolve. These effectful workflows must remain distinct from configuration and identity lookup.

ToolCallIdentity distinguishes untracked calls from missing thread identity and combines scope/thread/call with a fingerprint. LiveConversation validates an opaque handle before requesting resolution. Preserve scope and invalid-input semantics.

WorkspacePath expands a candidate then delegates containment to PathSafety and maps outside/unreadable errors. CodexSandboxPolicy handles explicitly supplied versus default policies separately. This pass does not prove path safety transitively or justify merging sandbox-policy construction with path resolution.

BridgePort accepts zero, searches alternatives only for the default port, and rejects occupied explicitly sourced ports. ProcessIdentity tries procfs then ps, returns unknown on exceptions and gone for invalid inputs; neither is an ordinary configuration default.

SourceFallback retains a separate availability map alongside fallback values. WeightFacts retains member facts, per-member freshness and race_signature. Keep fallback data distinguishable from current evidence.

Pricing resolves relationship evidence and preserves coverage reasons; RelationshipRegistry keys by provider/source/source version/relationship revision and distinguishes missing historic revisions. Replacing missing history with a current definition would change accounting semantics.

PriceTable.Window treats missing occurrence time as peak when a schedule exists; BalanceBaseline honors a configured deposit while warning if stale and otherwise may seed persisted state. These are deliberate domain policies requiring separate decisions.

Analytics.ScopeResolver returns session only for nil root, otherwise resolves a joinable root, members and boot-scoped usage intersection or unavailable. Preserve unavailable versus unfiltered-session scope.

Cadence, environment references, model selectors, backend configuration and prewarm resolution use different precedence and fallback rules. No new defect, universal resolver or saving is established by matching names.

reviewed_families.name: reconcile
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations plus available?/same_run?/same_scope? helpers in three presenters read; transitive state transitions and consumers remain outside this family pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: The name covers presentation retention, handshake completion, configuration recovery, claim recovery, subscription restoration, compaction and accounting. Shared reduction syntax does not establish a common state machine.
constraints: RunSummary and CurrentRunOutcomes have identical outer retention bodies but different available? helpers: summary additionally requires run.valid?. UsageSummary uses its own state predicate and scope equality. Any common retention combinator needs explicit availability and identity predicates; overlaps inherited web-occ-17 rather than a new finding.

InterruptHandshake requires both acknowledged interruption and observed idle, and limits completion to pause/operator_message actions. Preserve this two-part completion condition independently of other reconciliation loops.

StartupClaimReconciler distinguishes completed in-memory work, same-boot retry with recorded failures, same-boot marker without failures, new boot and unreadable marker. Unreadable marker retains claims; a same-boot restart does not blindly repeat release against a newly empty registry.

TicketDetail configuration reconciliation retains last-known-good state when configuration is unreadable and resets only through validated configuration. GraphProjection delegates to its own snapshot/failure policy. Preserve configuration uncertainty separately from a proven change.

Membership reconciliation marks unavailable when required observations fail. RateLimitFallback resolves configuration once, sorts running entries and bounds transitions per tick. These are distinct workload and failure policies.

Compaction reconciliation treats missing, valid/pending and corrupt manifests separately and quarantines corruption. RelationshipRegistry returns missing-revision evidence for absent historic definitions rather than substituting a current definition.

TicketContextSelection checks root and exact membership, retains surviving history and rotates requests on generation changes; AnalyticsRuntime suppresses duplicate loads and exposes distinct unavailable/unscopable states. Preserve scope revocation and inflight behavior.

Pane-border reconciliation invokes tmux changes; DecisionAttentionSignals synchronizes multiple classifications/expiry conditions; ExecutorBindings delegates subscription reconciliation. No universal pure reducer or side-effect policy is supported.
This pass does not certify convergence, retry safety or durable transition ordering. These require owner/helper/consumer validation and remain explicit synthesis obligations.

reviewed_families.name: changeset
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions read from frozen census/source; field declarations, default values, delegated validators and downstream settings remain outside this family pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: All inspected changesets belong to configuration schemas and use existing Ecto casting/validation. Repeated pipeline syntax is not evidence that another generic validator is needed or that configuration domains can share one policy.
constraints: All visible casts use empty_values: []; preserve explicit empty-value handling rather than silently restoring framework defaults during extraction. Field declarations and custom types still determine accepted values beyond these bodies.

Zero is permitted for selected disabling/unbounded/resource settings but rejected for others. Port validation also differs: Opencode applies an upper bound below 65536, while Server visibly checks only nonnegative values. Do not infer complete downstream validation or a reached bug from this difference alone.

Polling rejects legacy interval_ms keys by raising before casting, validates a minimum usage cadence and rejects unknown interval classes through a helper. Preserve migration diagnostics, units and failure mode.

Agent preprocesses uncapped max turns and scheduler defaults, then validates routing, backend selections, priority, fallback and complexity mappings. Validation order and known-backend dependencies belong in the package contract.

Toplevel schema composes embeds and adds raw nonnegative-integer checks for takeover alert hours. Github tracker validates credential IDs, identity mode, user lists, API budgets and endpoint concurrency through both visible checks and delegated helpers.

BuildOrder applies bounded values plus labels-cadence validation; Webhooks constrains widening to at least one; Decisions validates allowed kinds before normalizing. Keep cross-field and normalization order explicit.

Thin cast-only schemas are not automatically missing validation: custom field types, defaulting and later checks were not exhaustively inspected here. Completeness requires a separate end-to-end configuration audit.
No new defect or LOC saving is claimed. Package decomposition should retain domain-owned schemas and a deliberate composition boundary while reusing Ecto.

reviewed_families.name: new
reviewed_families.coverage: All literal definitions/declarations read from frozen census/source; struct defaults and transitive validators/runtime readers are not fully reviewed by this pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: New spans empty structs, normalized domain records, validated accounting envelopes, runtime dependency wiring and checkpoint restoration. Standard struct construction is already shared language machinery; common naming is not a new abstraction boundary.
constraints: CurrentRunProjections.State.new constructs unavailable source state, generation and restore-fence bookkeeping, then reads/restores a checkpoint. AgentList.State.new reads terminal geometry and prewarm state. These are not pure allocation functions.

GraphProjection.Options tracks separate attempted/successful labeled reads, authority epochs, pending/forced requests and task monitors. TicketDetail and TicketHistory options use different reset and configuration contracts. Preserve unknown authority and never-observed timestamps rather than substitute healthy defaults.

Catalog and SelectedRoot bound collection sizes and emit distinct diagnostics for overflow or malformed input. Member and RootSummary normalize related fields but carry different dependency, progress and diagnostic policies; shared field syntax alone does not prove equivalent helper behavior.

Membership.Event validates attributes, computes a checksum and checks recovery-record size. DecisionEvent validates a supplied durable event ID. UsageEnvelope validates schema, identity, epochs, dates, dimensions and measurement presence before returning a tagged result. Preserve these construction gates.

UsageLedger.Record validates positive bounded position and round-trips delta encoding/decoding; PriceTable and RelationshipRegistry validate catalogs and can return errors. Do not replace validated construction with unchecked struct allocation.

ProviderAccountGeneration.State initializes service continuity, tombstones and mint functions; Webhooks.DeliveryMode distinguishes configured_unproven from never_configured. Fresh allocation does not establish trust or delivery health.

CacheInspector.Entry measures age from fetched_at, separates validator/body presence and scrubs selected metadata. Preserve observation semantics and presentation disclosure independently of constructor reuse.
RouteState accepts a request epoch directly while TicketContextSelection normalizes it; lifecycle normalizes timestamps/state and boolean flags. Defaults and input acceptance remain domain-owned.
Empty-struct constructors may be intentional API ownership points. No new defect, generic constructor framework or LOC saving is established; full transitive validation remains open.

limits: Thirty-seven selected families and 1165 literal definitions/declarations reviewed. Remaining names and other high-frequency callbacks are not claimed reviewed. Name/body equality is not semantic duplication; overlap with body/raw reviews is non-additive. Transitive correctness and savings are not claimed.
next: Inspect high-frequency non-callback and lifecycle/state families; distinguish generic callback names from duplication evidence.
Complete label-state concept and constant sweeps.
Reconcile family proposals with inherited finding IDs and produce final duplication units.
